parsed.attack: The product asks for labour now against a benefit five years out, contingent on a Medicaid application that may never be filed and that an elder-law attorney would assemble anyway, and nothing in the product pushes back when a bill is skipped. The ignoring starts around the fourth or fifth document, when photographing one produces no visible result - no answer, no relief, just a line nobody reads - and skipping produces no visible result either, so the two become indistinguishable. Worse, the wedge explicitly starts the record at signup rather than importing history, so during the exact months when the first renewal is decided the switching cost it relies on does not yet exist: cancelling in month two throws away six bills.
parsed.strongest_defence: The near-term value is not the lookback at all, it is settling up between siblings, which is a live argument every month and gives the record a reason to be current; the lookback is why the record must be complete, not why the app gets opened. Bills arrive on their own schedule forever, so the trigger is external and permanent, and by month nine the accumulated evidence is genuinely unreproducible, which is the point at which the subscription stops being quittable.
parsed.verdict_reason: The monthly bill flow is a real external trigger, but the moat is five years deep and empty during the first-renewal window, and skipping a document carries no felt consequence.
